Gabin Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Gąbin, Poland

Demolished. Gąbin's Jewish cemetery, established in 1768, was devastated during the Nazi occupation — its tombstones used to harden roads and build curbs, and an anti-tank ditch cut through the grounds in 1944 — then left to decades of neglect as an illegal dump and informal football pitch after the war. A 1993 flood revealed tombstones that had been used to reinforce a nearby bridge, prompting a restoration effort by the descendants of Gąbin's Jews together with several heritage foundations and the town itself: the site was fenced and rededicated in 1999, with a lapidarium built from the recovered matzevot. The town's Jewish history includes Awraham Abele Gombiner, a 17th-century Talmudist whose commentary 'Magen Awraham' remains influential in Jewish law, and the poet Rejzel Żychlińska, a winner of the prestigious Itzik Manger Prize.
